items.transcript: One thing that people don't do because they think they're saving time by not doing but it's actually going to cost them more time is removing everything before they clean. Because otherwise you're just going to be doing this, putting it back on and it's going to be wet so that's going to create mold. Just take it off. If you can carry it safely, take it off. Unplug it. Just remove it, get it out of the way. Now if you cannot carry it safely to another location, just move it out of the way so you can clean under it. I hate housekeepers that just clean around things. It's literally one of my biggest pet peeves.

items.caption:
Do you dust before you start cleaning? You need to dust before cleaning that way you aren’t dragging around dust and hair when you’re cleaning!
•
#clean #dust #howto #tips #petpeeve
items.transcript: I think one of my biggest cleaning pet peeves as someone who used to be a professional housekeeper, and I also cleaned houses for over 10 years, is that I hate, hate, hate when people clean something without dusting it first. Listen, it's going to take you 10, 20 seconds to dust it with a Swiffer duster, but it's going to save you a bunch of time. Because if you don't dust first, you're just like spreading the dust back and forth. Or I hate when you're cleaning something and like a strand of hair is just like wet and you're just like moving it from side to side. All of that is avoidable if you just dust it first because the Swiffer duster is going to catch and grab all that hair and all that dust, making your job of cleaning much easier. So it's something that I learned early on when I started cleaning houses. Nobody taught me this, but I was like, I hate cleaning a toilet with like hair. So what do you do? You dust it first.
